decisions.reason: I wanted to learn AI by building a real-time screener end to end.
decisions.lesson: Stakeholder collaboration, clear requirements and documentation matter as much as code. The project taught me to think like a forward-deployed engineer.
decisions.title: Scope and audience
decisions.context: A freelance client project with a dual goal: a personalised stock screener for the client, and a product for investment enthusiasts.
decisions.decision: Built it as an incremental prototype over about 12 iterations across the frontend, backend, authentication and security.
decisions.result: Developed with Lovable, then worked on indexing and performance. Résumé-reported coverage: 5,300+ NSE and BSE stocks. Future ambition: open-source the project.

decisions.reason: Unlimited access and an earlier $40 tier were considered and not retained. Detailed reasoning: Upload needed.
decisions.title: Plans and pricing
decisions.context: The screener needed plans that worked for the client and for individual investors.
decisions.decision: Final plans: Free trial, Pro at about $5/month and Premium at about $20/month. The Free trial changed from 30 days to about 15 days. Annual billing carries an average 17% discount. Watchlist export and sharing apply to the paid plans, and Premium adds the portfolio dashboard.
decisions.result: Final plan structure documented. No paid subscriptions yet.

decisions.reason: Competitor research shaped the split, and gating limited abuse and API load.
decisions.title: Feature gating
decisions.context: Stock search, watchlists, Smart Alerts, OAuth sign-in and automatic price refresh had to be split across plans.
decisions.decision: Gated the portfolio dashboard and automatic refresh to Premium. Required registration, with limited trial access.
decisions.result: Plan-based access is in place. User response: Upload needed.

decisions.title: Payments approach
decisions.context: The product needed a payment provider for subscriptions.
decisions.decision: Selected Razorpay after considering Stripe and Juspay. Discarded manual bank transfers.
decisions.result: No paid subscriptions have occurred yet because development and deployment are incomplete.

decisions.lesson: Launching exposed discoverability, performance, cost and sustainability as product problems, not only engineering ones.
decisions.title: Launch
decisions.context: The screener moved from requirements to a public custom domain.
decisions.decision: Launched on a custom domain through Cloudflare.
decisions.result: Cloudflare reports traffic on equityiq.in, with significant United States and international request volume.
decisions.source: Source narrative; Cloudflare exports; all three résumés

decisions.lesson: Raw views do not equal users. Bot filtering, performance and hosting cost decide whether traffic is sustainable.

We pitched a regional voice-based system to help daily-wage workers with everyday communication and information needs. At NEC E-Summit 2024 at IIT Bombay, I pitched a job-matching app for daily-wage and off-season workers. Our team’s pitch ranked 4th in India, as reported in my résumés. The idea included regional-language support, salary-negotiation help and planned government welfare tie-ups for fair wages.

secret.story: During my cybersecurity internship at Edunet Foundation, I studied bit-level image steganography and built a GUI to hide and retrieve data. This puzzle applies that technique in the browser.
secret.grant: $3,000 is about ₹2,80,000 in India. I would spend about 40 to 50% on a new smartphone, wired earphones and essential accessories, and possibly a high-end laptop if my Wispr Flow work needs one. Otherwise, I would save the remainder toward a better future device.

receipts.title: The Autopsy
receipts.built: The client initially asked me to build a tool. I approached the requirement differently and developed a complete product end to end: cloud hosting, authentication, multi-user support, administrative access, user and analytics visibility, portfolio dashboards, subscription-based feature restrictions and role- and privilege-based access control. As admin, I could monitor users and application analytics; users reached dashboards and features according to their subscription tier and permissions. The client was satisfied, although I believe there was still room for improvement. The project is a starting point for my freelancing and software development career. Manual development, problem-solving and independent technical understanding will continue to remain valuable.

buildLog:
01 Ideation. Asked for 10 to 15 project ideas that solve real problems, each with problem, solution, existing solutions, gaps and MVP.
02 Simplified plan. Condensed the Out Loud concept and delivery plan into a buildable spec, with a prerequisites and requirements report.
03 First demo. Built the single-page structure: Hero, Autopsy, Voice-First Bharat, Secret Layer, Voice Receipts, Projects and Skills, About and Contact, with marked placeholders and a global animation toggle.
04 Design concepts. Requested three or four small design models before building, then chose one independent visual direction.
05 Refinement. Fixed the title glitch with a typing animation, added dark and light themes, replaced the word hunt with a three-image puzzle and removed carousels and marquees.
06 Private tools. Added the Content Setup tool, Voice Intro recording, one-page print summary and in-browser steganography decoder.
07 Source-of-truth refresh. Filled sections from the résumés and reference, moved audio and transcripts to a private editor, changed the font and removed promotional labels.
voiceLimit: Automatic corrections can change what I meant. Dictated text still needs editing. Accuracy drops with less familiar languages and words. Background noise affects recognition. Sensitive information should not be spoken aloud.
